questions.question_text:
Ava drinks $\frac{2}{7}$ L in the morning and $\frac{3}{7}$ L later.
How much altogether?

options.why: This adds the denominators as well as the numerators, giving $7+7=14$ on the bottom.
This subtracts the numerators, $3-2=1$, finding a difference instead of the total.
This subtracts the numerators AND adds the denominators, making both slips at once.

questions.question_text:
A roll has $\frac{11}{12}$ m left.
A piece of $\frac{5}{12}$ m is cut off.
How much remains?
Give the answer in simplest form.

options.why: This is equivalent but has not been simplified to the expected answer.
This adds the cut piece instead of subtracting it.

questions.question_text: Two ribbons measure $\frac{4}{15}$ m and $\frac{6}{15}$ m. What is their total length?

options.why: This subtracts the numerators, $6-4=2$, instead of adding the lengths.
This adds the denominators as well as the numerators, giving $\frac{10}{30}=\frac{1}{3}$.

questions.question_text:

What fraction is complete?
Give the answer in simplest form.

options.why: This is equivalent but has not been simplified.
This adds the denominators instead of keeping ninths.

questions.question_text: Three friends eat $\frac{5}{20}$, $\frac{4}{20}$ and $\frac{3}{20}$ of the same pizza. What fraction of the pizza is left?

options.why: This gives the fraction eaten, $\frac{12}{20}=\frac{3}{5}$, instead of the fraction left.
This adds the denominators when finding the fraction eaten, giving $\frac{12}{60}=\frac{1}{5}$, then subtracts that from the whole.

questions.question_text: Lena eats $\frac{7}{24}$ of a cake and Noah eats $\frac{11}{24}$ of the same cake. What fraction of the cake is left?

options.why: This gives the fraction eaten, $\frac{18}{24}=\frac{3}{4}$, instead of the fraction left.
This adds the denominators when finding the fraction eaten, giving $\frac{18}{48}=\frac{3}{8}$, then subtracts that from the whole.
